Getting started with mcbarycenter package

library(mcbarycenter)

Introduction

Placeholder description of the method. This section will be filled in with a more complete overview later.

mcbarycenter implements the method for calculating the quantile function of barycenters using both the empirical barycenter and the MCB estimator. The package also provides tools for calculating quantile differences, graphing results, and carrying out hypothesis tests to compare barycenters across groups of distributions.

Some functionality depends on external packages. In particular, REBayes and Rmosek can be used to make the NPMLE workflow run faster. We also use ideas from deconvolveR, but rewrote the relevant function to make it faster for the setting used in this package.

The examples below use the bundled sample_data data set.

data("sample_data")
head(sample_data)
#>   id      value
#> 1  1  1.2825057
#> 2  1 -0.8607872
#> 3  1  2.7440578
#> 4  1  3.7547658
#> 5  1  1.1531093
#> 6  2  3.6544903

Estimating the barycenter quantile function

Empirical Barycenter

The empbary() function computes empirical quantiles within each subject or group and then averages those quantiles across groups.

Arguments:

  • df: the input data frame.
  • id_col: the column identifying subjects or groups.
  • val_col: the column containing the numeric observations.
  • weight_col: an optional column containing group weights; if omitted, the empirical barycenter is unweighted.
  • alpha_grid: the grid of quantile levels to estimate.
  • quantile_type: the type argument passed to stats::quantile().

Example:

emp_res <- empbary(
  df = sample_data,
  id_col = "id",
  val_col = "value"
)

head(emp_res$res)
#>   quantile  estimate         se     ci_lo    ci_hi
#> 1     0.01 0.6728834 0.09770314 0.4813887 0.864378
#> 2     0.02 0.6728834 0.09770314 0.4813887 0.864378
#> 3     0.03 0.6728834 0.09770314 0.4813887 0.864378
#> 4     0.04 0.6728834 0.09770314 0.4813887 0.864378
#> 5     0.05 0.6728834 0.09770314 0.4813887 0.864378
#> 6     0.06 0.6728834 0.09770314 0.4813887 0.864378

Marginal-constructed barycenter

The mcbary() function estimates the barycenter quantile function using the marginal-corrected barycenter procedure.

Arguments:

  • df: the input data frame.
  • id_col: the column identifying subjects or groups.
  • val_col: the column containing the observed numeric values.
  • method: the mixture estimation method; options include "spline", "npmle", "raw", and "beta".
  • x_grid: the threshold grid to use when cutpoints is not supplied.
  • cutpoints: the number of evenly spaced thresholds constructed from the observed data range; either cutpoints or x_grid must be supplied.
  • bootstrap_samples: the number of bootstrap resamples used for uncertainty estimation.
  • alpha_grid: the grid of quantile levels to estimate.
  • use_midpoint: whether to use interval midpoints when constructing the quantile distribution.
  • estimate_endpoints: whether to estimate the endpoint support regions.
  • use_isotonic_dist: whether to enforce monotonicity on the cumulative mixture curves before converting them to quantile distributions.
  • use_isotonic_output: whether to enforce monotonicity on the final estimated quantile curve and confidence bounds.
  • weight_col: an optional column containing id-level weights.
  • progress: whether to display a bootstrap progress bar.
  • ci_level: the confidence level used for reported intervals.
  • ...: additional arguments passed to the mixture estimation routine.
bary_res <- mcbary(
  df = sample_data,
  id_col = "id",
  val_col = "value",
  method = "spline",
  cutpoints = 20,
  bootstrap_samples = 2,
  progress = FALSE
)

head(bary_res$res)
#>   quantile  estimate estimate_bs         se       ci_lo     ci_hi   pct_ci_lo
#> 1     0.01 0.2382460 -0.01098648 0.14012985 -0.03640345 0.5128954 -0.10511890
#> 2     0.02 0.2990117  0.08160117 0.06943718  0.16291732 0.4351061  0.03495665
#> 3     0.03 0.3174303  0.15380647 0.01643315  0.28522192 0.3496387  0.14276748
#> 4     0.04 0.3355905  0.21727565 0.02367705  0.28918436 0.3819967  0.20137055
#> 5     0.05 0.3648462  0.30032267 0.06542417  0.23661714 0.4930752  0.25637389
#> 6     0.06 0.3860502  0.34972302 0.08393996  0.22153092 0.5505695  0.29333623
#>    pct_ci_hi
#> 1 0.08314595
#> 2 0.12824570
#> 3 0.16484547
#> 4 0.23318074
#> 5 0.34427145
#> 6 0.40610981

The estimated quantile curve is stored in bary_res$res. The full object also contains bootstrap-based uncertainty summaries, the estimated mixing distributions, and the covariance matrix used by downstream comparison tools.

Graphing tools

The package includes helpers for plotting both the estimated barycenter quantiles and the intermediate mixing distributions.

graph_quantiles(bary_res)

graph_mixtures(bary_res)

Comparing barycenters

To compare barycenters across samples, we first estimate each barycenter on the same quantile grid and then apply equalbary_test(). The example below splits the sample by odd and even subject identifiers only to illustrate the workflow.

odd_ids <- unique(sample_data$id)[unique(sample_data$id) %% 2 == 1]
even_ids <- unique(sample_data$id)[unique(sample_data$id) %% 2 == 0]

sample_odd <- subset(sample_data, id %in% odd_ids)
sample_even <- subset(sample_data, id %in% even_ids)

bary_odd <- mcbary(
  sample_odd,
  id_col = "id",
  val_col = "value",
  method = "raw",
  cutpoints = 10,
  bootstrap_samples = 2,
  progress = FALSE
)

bary_even <- mcbary(
  sample_even,
  id_col = "id",
  val_col = "value",
  method = "raw",
  cutpoints = 10,
  bootstrap_samples = 2,
  progress = FALSE
)

graph_quantiles(odd = bary_odd, even = bary_even)

comparison <- equalbary_test(bary_odd, bary_even, B = 50, seed = 1)

comparison$sup_norm$pval
#> [1] 0.14
comparison$int_sq_norm$pval
#> [1] 0.46
comparison$hotelling$pval
#> [1] 0.834118
